findings.description: deliver is now a coroutine function, but flush calls it without await. The coroutine object is always truthy, so the branch is always taken and no message is ever sent (a 'coroutine was never awaited' warning is emitted). Lines are deleted from the queue as if delivered, so digests are silently lost and failed is always empty.
findings.title: Missing await on async deliver() makes every digest look delivered

findings.description: Once the await is added, flush yields at each send, so add() can run concurrently. `sorted(self._pending)` takes a snapshot of the keys, so recipients added during the flush are skipped (fine). But `self._pending[recipient]` at line 42 raises KeyError if the key was removed meanwhile, for example by a concurrent flush. Two concurrent flushes can also both send the same lines and then double-delete via `del lines[:sent]`.
findings.suggestion: Guard flush with an asyncio.Lock and use `self._pending.get(recipient)`, skipping recipients that no longer exist.
findings.title: Iterating the pending dict across awaits while add() can mutate it
